items.title: Bob Wilber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 1998
items.q: I was discovering, besides Benny Goodman I was going back and discovering Johnny Dodds, who played with Louis Armstrong, Frank Teschemacher, all these different players.

ctx.x: At what point did you learn how to play over the break?

Oh, well that took a little while. That took a little while. But at that point I already loved Benny Goodman so I said Jeez, maybe I could play like Benny. And I started, luckily my teacher at high school, the band director, was also an excellent clarinetist. That was his main instrument. He started me off with the standard exercises and books that any classical clarinet starts on. He was a good teacher.
